attacks.claim: Share links embed the owner's live project API key in the URL query (`k`), and the public share page returns it to any unauthenticated viewer as `replayKey`. Anyone with the link, including forwards and Slack/X unfurl crawlers, gets a working credential that spends the owner's quota (pro projects are billed per token). The key also leaks via browser history, Referer headers and proxy logs.
attacks.evidence: url.searchParams.set("k", project.apiKey); ... return { messages: share.messages, model: share.model, replayKey: url.searchParams.get("k") };

attacks.claim: Once links are posted publicly, the key exposure cannot be undone. Deleting a share only returns 404 and does not revoke or rotate the exposed key. The rollback only stops new signups, so it does not close the leak, and there is no key-rotation path.
attacks.evidence: Shares can be deleted from Playground → History; deleted shares return 404. ... Rollback: `free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working.

attacks.claim: Anonymous viewers replaying against the owner's project quota can drive unbounded per-token spend on paid projects. There is no per-share or per-viewer limit, and the changelog's 'even without a Lumen account' promise hides who is billed.
attacks.evidence: // Viewers without an account replay against the owner's project quota.

attacks.claim: The $4k/month hard budget is not enforced. The $3.6k estimate assumes 2 replicas, but the pool autoscales to 24 H100s at $2.49/h (about $43k/month). Signup is email-only with no card, and the only guards are a replica-count page at >6 and no spend alert or cap.
attacks.evidence: min_replicas: 2, max_replicas: 24, scale_on: queue_depth > 8 for 60s; "~$3.6k/month, within the $4k/month free-tier budget"; "free pool replicas > 6 pages on-call"

attacks.claim: The free tier has no `daily_tokens` limit in the config diff, although the release notes promise 100k tokens/day. With 4096 max tokens per request and a loose rate limit, the advertised cap is not enforced.
attacks.evidence: free block: rate_limit, max_tokens_per_request, pool only (no daily_tokens); release notes: "100k tokens per day"

attacks.claim: The shipped rate limit (20 per second, burst 40) is about 60x looser than the public promise of 20 per minute. QA ran against a staging config with `per: minute`, so the production limit was never tested.
attacks.evidence: rate_limit: { requests: 20, per: second, burst: 40 } vs "20 requests per minute" and "staging config used `per: minute`"

attacks.claim: Rollback and kill-switch coverage is inadequate. Turning off `free_signup_open` leaves existing free keys and share links working, so runaway load or spend cannot be shed. There is no budget or queue-depth alert and no launch-time capacity plan, and scale-out is reactive (a 60s trigger plus H100 start time) while the 17:00 UTC launch post follows signups opening at 16:45.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: `free_signup_open` off stops new signups; existing free keys keep working. / min_replicas: 2 ... scale_on: queue_depth > 8 for 60s

attacks.claim: The capacity claim of <30% utilization on two replicas has no throughput basis, load test or peak factor. The projection also ignores the HN/X launch spike and the many-accounts abuse case.
attacks.evidence: Two H100 replicas serve the projected free load at < 30% utilization

attacks.claim: Shared conversations are stored in full and are publicly readable, with no expiry, no retention policy, no warning to the sharer, and no redaction. Open Graph unfurls push the content to third-party crawlers, which deletion cannot recall. Behavior on account deletion is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: messages: session.messages ... Share pages are server-rendered with Open Graph tags so links unfurl nicely on Slack/X.

attacks.claim: Public free-tier signup has no stated privacy notice, retention or data-use statement for prompts, and no terms or age acceptance.
attacks.evidence: Sign up with email, no card required. ABSENT: retention period, privacy policy reference, terms acceptance
